title: As the Hart, with Eager Looks
description: As the Hart, with Eager Looks in Tonic Solfa to RATISBON (WERNER), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 226, “The Soul Thirsting for God”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to RATISBON (WERNER); any other Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: As the hart, with ea-ger looks, Pan-teth for the wa-ter brooks, So my soul, a-thirst for Thee, Pants the liv-ing God to see; When, O, when, with-out a fear, Lord, shall I to Thee draw near?

lines: As the hart, with eager looks,
So my soul, athirst for Thee,
Pants the living God to see;
When, O, when, without a fear,
Lord, shall I to Thee draw near?
Why art thou cast down, my soul?
God, thy God, shall make thee whole;
God shall lift thy fallen head,
Be the saving health of thine.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to RATISBON (WERNER) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
